newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies sharply after OPEC agrees freeze.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies sharply after OPEC agrees freeze.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures surged to new session highs in late trading on Wednesday breaking the psychological $18.00 barrier after Iran's oil minister said OPEC solved the issue of quota compliance, traders said.
OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman then said the producer group had agreed to a freeze of its 25.033 million barrels per day (bpd) ceiling for six months.
August Brent rose 56 cents a barrel to $18.43 by 1838 GMT and then eased back slightly to trade at $18.18.
It reversed its late afternoon trading trend in the red as NYMEX rose but then lost steam.

Lukman also said the group's members had agreed to go back to their production allocations and added that "no threats" had been made to overproducers. He confirmed all individual quotas have been left unchanged.
"It's the OPEC news pushing the market up," one trader said.
"But I don't now how big the volumes are exactly or if it will last," she added.
Lukman said that ministers expected the meeting to be wrapped up on Thursday when they meet again at 0800 GMT.

OPEC President Abdullah Salem al-Badri, the Libyan oil minister, told reporters: "We had a frank discussion and one by one everyone agreed to adhere to quota over the next six months, and now the markets will judge".
August Brent had continued to trade near the session lows at $17.70 before rallying on the OPEC news.
